10    A.  Discovery Standards                                                 
11    Under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, parties may generally obtain discovery regarding 
12  any non-privileged matter that is relevant to any party's claim or defense and proportional to the 
13  needs of the case.  Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(1).  Information need not be admissible at trial to be 
14  discoverable.  Id.                                                        

15    Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 37(a)(1) provides that, in part:        
16       On notice to other parties and all affected persons, a party may move for an order 
        compelling disclosure or discovery. The motion must include a certification that 
17       the movant has in good faith conferred or attempted to confer with the person or 
        party failing to make disclosure or discovery in an effort to obtain it without court 
18       action.                                                              

19       Western District of Washington Local Civil Rule 37(a) requires parties “meet and confer” 
20  by making a “good faith” effort to reach an agreement including through a “face-to-face meeting 
21  or a telephone conference.”  LCR 37(a).                                   
22       Further, under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(c)(1), the Court may, for good cause, 
23  issue a protective order for a party from whom discovery is sought to shield “a party or person 
24                                                                            
1  from annoyance, embarrassment, oppression, or undue burden or expense.”  Fed. R. Civ. P. 
2  26(c)(1).  Like motions to compel discovery, motions for a protective order “must include a 
3  certification, in the motion or in a declaration or affidavit, that the movant has engaged in a good 
4  faith meet and confer conference with other affected parties in an effort to resolve the dispute 

5  without court action.”  LCR 26(c)(1).                                     
6       Plaintiff’s telephone calls with Defendants’ counsel before filing its Motions to Compel 
7  satisfy the meet-and-confer requirement.  (Dkt. Nos. 58 at 1 n.2; 110 at 2 n.1.)  Although 
8  Defendants provide no certification, Plaintiff’s counsel confirms that she conferred with 
9  Defendants’ counsel by phone regarding Defendants’ Motion for a Protective Order prior to its 
10  filing.  (Dkt. No. 102 at 2.)  Therefore, Defendants also satisfy the meet-and-confer requirement.
